reviewRequired.note: Brownian motion is the likely intended term: irregular motion of small suspended particles caused by collisions with surrounding molecules. “Random movement of particles” alone is ambiguous.
Plasma is intended; it need not exist only at extremely high gas temperatures. Nonthermal plasmas also exist.
Thermal energy/particle kinetic energy is intended; the source’s wording is imprecise because particles do not stop moving when a material is cold.
Atoms/molecules/ions as appropriate. “Particles” is the generic intended school term; not all matter consists only of molecules.
Plasma is intended. The claimed universal6000°C threshold is false; plasmas can occur in nonthermal conditions and have no single threshold.
Vaporisation is likely intended as the broader liquid→gas term; evaporation is a specific surface process, not a perfect synonym for every vaporisation process.
Mist/fog/visible cloud droplets. If “steam” is intended in everyday usage, distinguish visible condensed droplets from invisible gaseous water vapour.
Melting is intended for externally heated solid surfaces, but melting need not always begin at an outside edge under every heating configuration.
Vaporisation; accept evaporation where surface escape is specifically meant, or boiling where bubbles form throughout the liquid.
